intro.title: Type async state idle loading success error
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple application that fetches data from an API and displays different UI states based on the request status. You will learn how to model asynchronous operations using a typed state object that tracks 'idle', 'loading', 'success', and 'error' statuses. The main technologies involved are TypeScript's union types and interfaces to ensure type safety. This approach helps manage UI updates and error handling in a predictable way, making your code more robust and maintainable.
intro.usecase: Managing async states is crucial for building responsive user interfaces that communicate status clearly. In real applications, you'll see this pattern when loading dashboard data, submitting forms, or fetching search results—each requiring distinct UI feedback. For example, a weather app shows a loading spinner while fetching forecasts, displays data on success, or shows an error message if the network fails. Implementing typed async states ensures your components handle all possible outcomes predictably, preventing bugs and improving user experience.
